nodes.name: ANALYSIS.md
nodes.summary: Reports a hardware-grounded TensorNet2 GPU profiling study on consumer Blackwell, combining PyTorch Profiler, Nsight Systems, and Nsight Compute results to identify launch-, occupancy-, and memory-bound regimes. It concludes that all-pairs Coulomb evaluation is the main large-system target, recommends Triton fusion and algorithmic long-range methods, and leaves the already-fused Warp backbone alone.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown uses quantitative tables, staged profiler evidence, ablation results, and explicit optimization recommendations to connect software operators with GPU hardware counters.

nodes.name: PAPER.md
nodes.summary: Working workshop-paper draft presenting a regime-to-remedy characterization of TensorNet2 on an RTX 5070 Laptop and selective BF16 precision for its learned-charge Coulomb path. It reports speed, memory, accuracy, equivariance, CUDA-graph, and batching results while positioning algorithmic long-range electrostatics as future work.
nodes.languageNotes: The draft follows a conventional scientific-paper structure and uses cross-referenced sections and quantitative tables to distinguish measured contributions from existing methods and future work.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Entry-point guide for reproducing the TensorNet2 GPU profiling study, describing the environment, harness, profiler wrappers, run order, and inference controls. It also records autograd, Warp-path, profiling-permission, and 8 GB VRAM constraints needed to interpret and reproduce the analysis.
